author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both the HTML vet page and the reinstated machine-readable /vets list accept an optional specialty query parameter, returning only veterinarians holding that whole, case-insensitive specialty name. Empty/whitespace behaves as absent; no match yields an empty list with a normal response.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when /vets.html?specialty=<name> is opened, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed and the page count reflects only them
Given a filtered page beyond the first, when a paging link is followed, then the link carries the specialty so the filtered list stays navigable
Given a specialty differing from a held specialty only by letter case, when the page or the machine-readable list is filtered by it, then it matches
Given a value that is a leading part of a held specialty but not the whole name, when either surface is filtered by it, then it matches no veterinarian
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is filtered by it, then the ordinary page or list is returned with no veterinarians and no error (HTTP 200)
Given a blank or whitespace-only specialty, when either surface is requested with it, then the result equals requesting that surface without the parameter
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when /vets?specialty=<name> is requested, then the machine-readable list returns only those veterinarians
Given no specialty parameter, when either surface is requested, then it behaves as it does today
The /vets machine-readable list is documented as a supported surface; the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is not reused
non_goals: Any on-screen control, form, or dropdown for choosing a specialty
notes: Narrows NG-9 (see adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md). Reinstates /vets as a supported surface; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, id not reused. Depends on REQ-VET-001. Matching is on the whole Specialty name, case-insensitive. system-design.md (owned by system-design-expert) still lists /vets as an unrequested artifact and REQ-VET-002-only; those Contracts rows and the open item need updating during design triage. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR (outside product-requirements-expert write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing vet-package controller pattern (system-design.md#contracts): VetController already reads from the cached VetRepository and paginates with PageRequest/PageImpl. This slice adds an optional `specialty` query parameter to both existing routes plus a thin in-memory filter step over the cached full collection. No new module, no new type, no new pattern; the `Vets` wrapper and the cache are reused as-is. IDE oracle not connected on this run; covering code verified by direct Read of VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, Specialty.java, and templates/vets/vetList.html (weaker basis than a resolved symbol, but the sources were read in full).
integration_points: /vets.html gains @RequestParam(required=false) specialty; filter is applied to the cached full collection BEFORE paging so totalPages/totalItems reflect only matches; build the page with PageImpl(pageContent, PageRequest.of(page-1, pageSize), filtered.size())
/vets (machine-readable) filters the full collection then wraps it in Vets; the existing $.vetList JSON shape is unchanged

vetList.html: add a `specialty` model attribute and rewrite the five paging links from the literal @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} form to Thymeleaf param syntax @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} so the parameter is carried across pages and omitted when blank

patterns.description: existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel pattern the filtered path mirrors — reuse PageRequest + PageImpl rather than a new repository query
Vet.getSpecialties() already returns specialties sorted by name; the match predicate reads getName() on each — stable order (PRD edge case 1) is preserved for free

risks.risk: Pushing case-insensitive matching to a repository/DB query would reproduce the REQ-OWN-002 known defect (vendor collation divergence: PostgreSQL is case-sensitive) on a new surface
risks.mitigation: Match in Java with getName().equalsIgnoreCase(trimmed) over the cached collection — vendor-independent and exactly the whole-name, case-insensitive, non-prefix contract REQ-VET-003 specifies

risks.risk: A repository method keyed by specialty would multiply @Cacheable("vets") cache entries per user-supplied value, case variant, and page number (unbounded, user-controlled keys)
risks.mitigation: Filter in-memory over the single cached findAll() result; the seeded collection is tiny and already fully cached, so no per-value cache key is created

risks.risk: Blank/whitespace must equal the no-parameter behavior, and the no-parameter path must behave exactly as today
risks.mitigation: Branch on StringUtils.hasText(specialty): when absent keep the existing findAll(pageable) path unchanged; only when present switch to findAll()+filter+PageImpl. Trim before matching

notes: Verdict minor, not new: no ADR warranted for the filter-location choice — it is controller-local and reversible, and the product decision already carries its non-goal ADR (2026-08-23-non-goal-veterinarian-search). Rationale for in-memory filtering is recorded in this record's risks rather than as "why" prose in system-design.md (state-vs-history discipline). Doc updates applied this dispatch: system-design.md Contracts — Vets row Implements now REQ-VET-003, VetController row now REQ-VET-001+REQ-VET-003 with filter noted; removed the stale Known Defects row calling /vets an unrequested route pending removal (it now serves REQ-VET-003; the "Three kinds of —" intro is now exactly accurate). adr/README.md gained the index row for the new non-goal ADR. Two notes for the implementer: (1) VetRepository.java is listed in the prd-entry file_targets but under the chosen in-memory design it likely needs NO change — treat it as a supporting path to confirm, not a required edit; do not add a specialty-keyed cached query. (2) The existing VetControllerTests uses @MockitoBean, which sits in tension with the project's no-mocks testing policy; that is a test-authoring call for the implementer/test-reviewer, not a design blocker — flagging only for awareness.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No SQL injection: filterBySpecialty compares the user-supplied specialty in-memory via equalsIgnoreCase over vetRepository.findAll() (no-arg); the value reaches no query on either surface
No unbounded/user-controlled cache keys: @Cacheable is keyed on the no-arg findAll(); filtering is in-memory so no per-value/case/page cache entries are created

No reflected XSS in paging links: specialty flows only into Thymeleaf @{...(specialty=${specialty})} URL expressions, which URL-encode query params and auto-escape attribute output; blank/whitespace maps to null and the param is omitted
Machine-readable /vets does not reflect the specialty into its JSON output
No dependency delta: build.gradle unchanged in the diff, so no new supply-chain surface

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test only exercises /vets.html?specialty=RADIOLOGY. PRD acceptance criterion 3 explicitly says the case-insensitive match must hold on both the page and the machine-readable list ("when the page or the machine-readable list is filtered by it, then it matches"). The /vets?specialty=RADIOLOGY JSON surface is untested. The implementation uses a shared filterBySpecialty helper, so the risk of divergence is low, but a future refactor that introduces a surface-specific code path would break the contract silently — no test would catch it.
findings.fix: Add a second mockMvc.perform call for get("/vets").param("specialty", RADIOLOGY.toUpperCase()).accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON) and assert jsonPath("$.vetList.length()").value(RADIOLOGY_VET_COUNT) in theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchCaseInsensitively, mirroring the pattern already used in theBlankSpecialtyShouldBehaveAsAbsent.

findings.description: The test only exercises /vets.html?specialty=radio. PRD acceptance criterion 4 says the prefix must match no veterinarian on either form ("when either form is filtered by it, then it matches no veterinarian"). The /vets JSON surface is untested for prefix non-match. Same refactor-risk argument applies as finding 1.
findings.fix: Add a second mockMvc.perform call for get("/vets").param("specialty", RADIOLOGY.substring(0, 5)).accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON) and assert jsonPath("$.vetList.length()").value(0) in theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchOnPrefix.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The in-memory filter path (filterBySpecialty over findAll()) is not self-evidently correct. A cold reader will reasonably ask why a repository query was not added instead. The design-block for REQ-VET-003 records the reasons: a per-value repository query would create unbounded cache entries keyed by user-supplied specialty values and case variants; a vendor-level query would reproduce the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity collation defect on a new surface. Neither reason is visible in the code.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment immediately before the filterBySpecialty call: // Filter in memory: avoids unbounded per-value cache entries and vendor collation divergence (see design-block for REQ-VET-003).

findings.description: The specialty value stored in the model, and thereby carried in all paging link URLs, is the raw (untrimmed) parameter string. filterBySpecialty trims internally, so filtering is correct, but paging URLs will contain encoded leading/trailing whitespace in the edge case where the caller supplied them. Trimming once at the handler entry point and using the trimmed value for both the model attribute and findPaginated would consolidate the concern in one place and make filterBySpecialty trivially correct without its own trim.
findings.fix: Replace lines 50-52 with: String activeSpecialty = StringUtils.hasText(specialty) ? specialty.trim() : null; Page<Vet> paginated = findPaginated(page, activeSpecialty); model.addAttribute("specialty", activeSpecialty);

approved_aspects: filterBySpecialty uses a stream pipeline with equalsIgnoreCase — correct whole-name case-insensitive match per PRD
PageImpl constructed with filtered.size() as total-element count — page count correctly reflects only matching vets
StringUtils.hasText used consistently at both handler entry points to treat null, empty, and whitespace-only as absent
Math.min(start + pageSize, filtered.size()) and start >= filtered.size() guards are correct subList bounds
Early return for the no-specialty path preserves the pre-existing paginated repository query unchanged
filterBySpecialty accepts Collection<Vet> rather than List<Vet> — correctly widened for both call sites
vetList.html paging links use Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} URL expressions that omit null params — correct approach for the no-specialty case
Constructor injection, no @Autowired — follows Spring Boot idiom
No prohibited naming suffixes, no abbreviations, no type-name repetition in method names

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: REQ-VET-003 is missing a mandatory Design Rationale link. The prd-authoring skill states Design Rationale is mandatory whenever an ADR records the decision behind the requirement. The non-goal ADR (2026-08-23-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md) records the boundary decision that admits specialty filtering into scope. A reader who navigates directly to REQ-VET-003 via a cross-reference from system-design.md finds no path to that decision document. The NG-9 preamble references the ADR but is not a substitute for a per-requirement link where the format spec requires one.

One sentence in the Context section exceeds the 30-word limit (37 words). Writing standards require sentences under 30 words: Filtering a list by a value it already displays is not the same capability as free-text search: it demonstrates a query the directory does not yet show, without reintroducing the paged prefix-search pattern owner search already teaches.
findings.fix: Filtering a list by a value it already displays is not the same capability as free-text search. It demonstrates a query the directory does not yet show, without reintroducing the paged prefix-search pattern owner search already teaches.

author: change-grader
summary: filter vet list by specialty on /vets.html and /vets

blast_radius.note: True slice is one controller, one Thymeleaf template, one test, plus four docs; code stays inside the vet module with no sensitive paths. The row overcounts (11 files/98 hunks) only because base b67f301 pulls in the unrelated harness-install commit a7d7cb6 (settings.json, .gitignore, CLAUDE.md, layout.toml); those are not this slice.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: filterBySpecialty uses equalsIgnoreCase for whole-name case-insensitive non-prefix matching; the in-memory paging path guards subList bounds (start>=size to empty, Math.min for end) and builds PageImpl with filtered.size() so page counts reflect matches; blank/whitespace resolves to null via hasText and takes the unchanged early-return path. No inverted operator, off-by-one, or hidden behavior change.

test_adequacy.note: Tests replace MockitoBean with a real seeded InMemoryVetRepository (no-mocks compliant) and assert discriminating outcomes: totalItems counts, jsonPath lengths, both HTML and JSON surfaces for case-insensitive and prefix-non-match, blank-as-absent, and the paging link carrying specialty=radiology. reviewer_hedging.note: Final round is clean unanimous approval with empty findings from all four reviewers; round-1 changes were fixable/autofix and re-approved. scope_deviation.note: design_revisions=0, consultations=0, build_retries=0. Change matches the requirement surface; VetRepository was listed in file_targets but correctly left unchanged under the in-memory design (a within-scope narrowing, not a wander).
